newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S ZUMA THREATENS TOBACCO ADVERTISING BAN.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S ZUMA THREATENS TOBACCO ADVERTISING BAN.

text.p: South African Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma on Thursday threatened to ban cigarette advertising if tobacco companies continued to flout strict regulations.
Answering questions in the Senate, she said that Rembrandt, United Tobacco Company, RJR Reynolds and Premier Tobacco were not meeting the requirements laid down by her ministry.
Their transgressions included "posting billboards with warnings that were not visible at night or do not show the nicotine or tar content as per regulation," Zuma said.
The companies were also "advertising in newspapers and magazines with adverts which do not show warnings of the correct size and do not have the tar and nicotine content."
She said her department was "taking action" against the companies and had "submitted charges" to the police.
"The matter is still receiving attention...but, of course, if they continue to ignore regulations, we will ban advertising," she said.
